items.title: 68251_Teddy McRae oral history interview
items.q: "I was always Chick -- Chick always say (inaudible) when he heard me, 'You're my next tenor player, man.'"

ctx.x: You know, one of the books I did for Life & Time, I think I showed you an article that -- we always, like (inaudible) the whole time we was with Chick, the union scale up there was around about fifty-five dollars. That was considered big money.

ctx.x: But they had set up a jam session just for Chick. And we cut -- Chick and I sat in the auditorium trying to duck somebody -- didn't want to
see somebody. So when we got over there, they say, "Come on, we're waiting for you downstairs." We went down there and all these top musicians were down there.
They had this jam session -- (inaudible) drummers about four or five drummers down there. Boy these guys could play // said there (inaudible) Chick (inaudible). They were just entertaining Chick.
